problem_type: renderer lifecycle writes split a canvas undo transaction
symptom: A multi-shot materialization correctly created four nodes and one group as a single transaction in the store, but after the real React renderer mounted those nodes, one Cmd+Z left all four nodes and the group on the canvas.
direct_cause: Node mount and reconciliation effects wrote default model, supplier, archetype, and video-aspect metadata through updateNode without disabling edit history. updateNode therefore opened new user-edit barriers after the materialization barrier even though no user edit had occurred.
class_root: Automatic renderer normalization and explicit user edits shared the same history-defaulting write path without declaring their different undo intent, allowing lifecycle timing to change the document's user-visible undo granularity.
affected_population: Users undoing a newly materialized multi-shot batch after its generation cards rendered
Users undoing a manual model or reference change followed by automatic supplier, archetype, or aspect reconciliation
Users opening legacy or partially initialized generation nodes whose metadata is healed on mount
entry_points: Default model selection after generation-model preferences load
Supplier identity and capability declaration reconciliation
Automatic video aspect selection after model or reference changes
internal_only_reason: Undo granularity and renderer lifecycle ownership are internal canvas contracts. Provider documentation cannot determine whether automatic metadata normalization is a separate user edit; the canvas transaction model and real Electron behavior are the deciding evidence.
invariants: Automatic renderer metadata normalization persists and emits its document events without creating an undo barrier of its own.
A user action and its synchronous or deferred automatic normalization undo as one user-visible step.
A materialized batch remains one undo step after its real generation-node components mount and initialize.
Explicit user changes to model, supplier, parameters, prompt, or title continue to create user-edit history.
Automatic reconciliation remains idempotent and does not suppress persistence or the canvas event journal.

recurrence.reason: Every generation card mount, legacy-node heal, supplier disconnect, or reference-driven normalization could create a new history barrier after an unrelated user action.
same_class_scan: Scanned generation-node mount effects and updateNode meta writes for automatic model, supplier, variant, archetype, and aspect normalization.
Separated automatic normalization callers from explicit model, supplier, prompt, title, and parameter edit handlers.
Exercised a four-node materialization with real mounted generation cards and result attachment before the first Undo.

prevention.strategy: Declare history intent at every shared automatic normalization write while leaving persistence and event journaling enabled.

migration: No project migration is required. Existing metadata remains valid; only the history intent attached to future automatic normalization writes changes.
residual_risks: A future renderer effect that writes prompt, title, or meta without history: false can reintroduce the same class of bug; the real Electron transaction walkthrough remains the end-to-end guard.
Automatic normalization events remain in the append-only canvas journal by design, so persistence and crash recovery continue to observe the normalized state.
